what: Impinj makes RAIN RFID chips and readers: tiny radio tags that let retailers, logistics companies and manufacturers identify and track individual items wirelessly. Its Monza and M800 tag chips go into labels on clothing, parcels and auto parts, and its readers and software capture the data.
customers: Label makers such as Avery Dennison, retailers including Walmart, apparel brands, airlines and logistics firms.
money: Chips sold to inlay and label makers, priced per chip.
moat: Impinj is the leading supplier of RAIN RFID tag chips and holds key patents, which it has enforced against rivals. Being designed into retailers’ systems gives it scale advantages.
risks: Revenue stalled in 2025 at $361M as inventory corrections hit tag chip orders.
Profits are thin and swing between small gains and losses.
Dependence on a few large label makers and retailers.
The forward P/E of about 88 prices in a lot of growth.
opportunities: Adoption is spreading from apparel to food, parcels and logistics, a far larger market.
Free cash flow has been positive since 2024.
Nine analysts average a target above $200.
Its M800 chips lower cost per tag, which widens the uses.
watch: Tag chip volumes and new uses in food and logistics.
view: Impinj is a bet on RFID tags becoming as common as barcodes. Retail apparel has adopted them, and the next wave, groceries, parcels and logistics, could multiply volumes. The company has shown the economics can work: free cash flow has been positive since 2024.

But growth has been uneven: revenue stalled in 2025 as customers worked through inventory, and profits remain thin. At about 88 times forward earnings, the market is paying for the next wave of adoption before it shows up.

This turns on whether food and logistics adoption arrives on time. I think the long-term case is strong but the valuation already reflects much of it, and the shares are volatile on any quarterly miss. I would wait for a better entry.
bull: Food and logistics adopt RFID at scale and tag volumes surge.
bear: Adoption is slower than hoped and the premium valuation contracts.
